high.title: SBV and US Treasury Issue Joint Statement on Monetary Policy
high.summary: The State Bank of Vietnam (SBV) and US Treasury have issued a joint statement reaffirming their commitment to avoid currency manipulation under IMF guidelines. Key agreements include: avoiding macroeconomic measures or capital controls that target exchange rates for competitive purposes; ensuring government investment tools like pension funds seek risk-adjusted returns and diversification rather than targeting exchange rates; and recognizing FX intervention as appropriate for addressing both appreciation and depreciation pressures to manage volatility and maintain macroeconomic stability. This statement is crucial for VND traders as it provides official clarity on Vietnam's FX policy framework and reduces risks of future US currency manipulation designations. The commitment to avoid competitive devaluation should support VND stability, while the acknowledgment of intervention rights gives SBV policy flexibility. Watch for how this affects US-Vietnam trade relations and FX market sentiment.

high.title: SBV Relaxes Real Estate Credit Room Requirements
high.summary: SBV has issued a directive to 25 commercial banks adjusting real estate credit growth calculations to support social housing and industrial park lending. From January 1-December 31, 2026, banks will not need to count increased lending balances (compared to end-2025) for social housing, industrial parks, and export processing zones toward total real estate credit when controlling sector growth rates. This applies to major banks including VietinBank, Agribank, BIDV, MSB, Sacombank, Techcombank, and others. This policy change is significant for the banking sector as it effectively increases available lending capacity for priority real estate segments. Banks with strong social housing and industrial financing capabilities should benefit most. The move supports government housing and industrial development goals while potentially boosting bank lending growth and fee income in these segments.

high.title: One Banking Stock Hit by Massive Foreign Selling of Nearly 2,000 Billion VND in Late May
high.summary: In the final week of May (25-29), the VN-Index experienced strong volatility around 1,860-1,890 points before closing down 13.64 points (-0.73%) at 1,863.49. Foreign investors continued heavy selling pressure with 5,118 billion VND net selling across the entire market over 5 sessions. MSB was the biggest target with 1,756 billion VND in net foreign selling, far exceeding other stocks, followed by HPG (-549 billion VND) and VHM (-423 billion VND). This massive foreign exodus from MSB specifically signals potential concerns about the bank's fundamentals or broader foreign investor sentiment toward Vietnamese banking stocks. The scale of selling pressure suggests institutional repositioning rather than retail activity. VND weakness could follow if foreign selling continues, while the banking sector may face valuation pressure. Monitor MSB's upcoming earnings and any corporate developments that might explain this targeted selling.

medium.title: SBV Wants to Amend Decree 24, Gold Market Faces Major Changes
medium.summary: SBV proposes removing gold jewelry production and trading from conditional business activities list, simplifying market entry requirements. This regulatory relaxation could impact gold trading dynamics and pricing mechanisms in the domestic market.

medium.title: SBV Speaks on Vinhomes' Gold-for-Housing Exchange Program
medium.summary: SBV requires Vinhomes to comply with all relevant laws when implementing gold-for-real estate exchange programs, including banking, foreign exchange, and consumer protection regulations. The central bank reaffirms its policy against using gold as payment means.

medium.title: Gold Prices for Bars and Plain Rings on May 29 Afternoon
medium.summary: Gold prices reversed sharply lower by afternoon May 29, dropping about 1.5 million VND per tael. SJC gold quoted at 155.5-158.5 million VND/tael, while international gold traded around $4,509/ounce. The volatility reflects continued uncertainty in global gold markets.

medium.title: 28 Banks Work Day and Night: 100,000 VND Transfers for Millions of Vietnamese - System Passes Unprecedented Test After a Decade of Digitization
medium.summary: Vietnam's banking system successfully handled the government's 100,000 VND social welfare transfer program, processing millions of transactions nationwide. This demonstrates the maturity of Vietnam's digital banking infrastructure and payment systems after a decade of digitization efforts.

medium.title: Securities Industry Enters Revaluation Cycle, Bank-Backed Firms to Benefit Significantly
medium.summary: NSI forecasts securities industry debt could rise at least 40% in 2026, with bank-backed securities firms positioned to benefit from easier access to funding. The sector expansion aligns with government GDP growth targets and minimum 15% credit growth expectations.
